card.summary_ko: 박지원의 한문 단편 〈양반전〉 전문. 환곡 천 섬을 갚지 못해 옥에 갇히게 된 정선의 가난한 양반이 신분을 부자에게 팔지만, 군수가 작성한 두 번째 매매 문서를 듣고 부자가 “나를 도둑으로 만들 셈이냐” 하며 달아난다.
card.summary_en: The complete Yangban-jeon (Tale of the Yangban), a classical-Chinese short story by Park Ji-won. A poor yangban of Jeongseon, unable to repay 1,000 seok of state grain loans, sells his rank to a rich man; on hearing the second deed of sale the rich man refuses, protesting that he is being made a thief.
card.edition_ko: 한국어 위키문헌 「연암집/제8권 별집」 (개정 413307, 2025-10-17)에서 〈兩班傳〉 한 편만 수록 — 작품 전문(맨 앞의 위키문헌 표제 ‘== 兩班傳 ==’ 포함, 한 문단으로 이어짐), 원저작 퍼블릭 도메인, 전사 CC BY-SA 4.0, 원문만·번역 없음. 첫 매매 문서의 첫머리에 전사자가 입력하지 못한 글자 표시(▼)가 하나 있다.
card.edition_en: Korean Wikisource 「연암집/제8권 별집」 (revision 413307, 2025-10-17): the single tale 兩班傳 only, complete from first to last sentence (including Wikisource's stray heading '== 兩班傳 ==' at the start, all in one paragraph); original in the public domain, transcription CC BY-SA 4.0. Original text only, no translation. One placeholder (▼) marks a character the transcriber could not enter at the start of the first deed.

notes.ko:
**저자** 박지원(1737–1805, 호 연암)은 반남 박씨로 서울의 노론 명문 양반 집안 출신입니다. 젊어서 과거를 포기하고 홍대용, 박제가, 이덕무 등과 어울리며 청의 발전된 문물을 배우자는 북학을 주장한 북학파의 대표입니다. 한때 홍국영의 정치적 압박을 피해 황해도 연암골에 숨어 살아 호가 연암이 되었습니다. 1780년 청 건륭제 칠순 축하 사절의 일원으로 중국에 다녀와 《열하일기》를 썼습니다. 늦게 음직으로 출사하여 안의현감, 면천군수, 양양부사 등을 지냈습니다. 정조의 문체반정(1792) 때 《열하일기》의 문체가 문제 되어 자송문을 지어 올리라는 요구를 받았다고 전합니다. 1805년에 세상을 떠났습니다. 〈양반전〉은 그가 열여덟~스무 살 무렵인 1755년경 쓴 신분 풍자 소설입니다.

**시대적 맥락** 〈양반전〉은 《방경각외전》에 실린 초기 한문 단편으로, 정확한 창작 연대는 확실하지 않으며 학계에서는 대체로 1750년대 중반 무렵으로 봅니다. 18세기 조선은 상공업과 화폐 경제가 성장하고 신분제가 흔들리며, 돈으로 양반 신분을 사는 일(납속·족보 매매)이 늘고 있었습니다. 이 소설은 환곡 빚에 몰려 양반 신분을 부자에게 파는 이야기를 통해 양반의 허례와 특권을 풍자합니다. 《연암집》에 실려 전하며, 조선 후기 신분제 비판과 실학 정신을 보여 주는 작품으로 읽혀 왔습니다.

**배경**
박지원(朴趾源, 1737–1805, 호 연암)은 조선 후기 북학파를 대표하는 문인이다. 〈양반전〉은 그가 젊은 시절에 쓴 한문 단편을 모은 《방경각외전(放璚閣外傳)》에 실린 한 편으로, 이 책은 《연암집》 별집으로 전한다. 정확한 창작 연도는 확실하지 않으며, 위키문헌 머리말은 《방경각외전》을 ‘젊었을 때 쓴 초기 작품집’이라 소개한다. 학계에서는 대체로 1750년대 중반, 그가 스무 살 안팎이던 때의 작품으로 본다.

**내용 (이 판 전체)**
이 판에는 〈양반전〉 한 편이 처음부터 끝까지 들어 있다.
- 발단: 정선 고을에 책읽기를 좋아하는 양반이 있어 새 군수가 올 때마다 직접 찾아가 예를 표한다. 그러나 집이 가난해 해마다 관청 곡식(환곡)을 꾸어 먹다가 쌓인 빚이 천 섬에 이른다. 순시하던 관찰사가 이를 알고 크게 노해 양반을 가두라 명하지만, 군수는 그를 불쌍히 여겨 가두지 못한다. 양반은 밤낮으로 울기만 하고, 아내는 “평생 글만 읽더니 환곡 갚는 데는 소용없다. 양반이 한 푼어치도 못 된다”고 꾸짖는다.
- 거래: 마을의 부자가 “양반은 가난해도 늘 높임을 받는데, 우리는 부유해도 천하다”며 양반 신분을 사기로 하고 환곡을 대신 갚는다. 놀란 군수가 찾아가자, 양반은 벙거지에 짧은 옷으로 땅에 엎드려 ‘소인’을 자처하며 신분을 팔았다고 말한다. 군수는 부자를 칭찬하고, 사사로운 거래는 분쟁의 씨앗이므로 고을 사람들을 증인으로 세워 문서를 만들자고 한다.
- 첫 문서: 향소와 좌수·별감이 증인으로 서고, 양반이 지켜야 할 번거로운 행실을 늘어놓는다. 새벽에 일어나 책을 외고, 굶주림과 추위를 참되 가난을 입에 올리지 말고, 돈을 만지지 말고 쌀값을 묻지 말고, 소를 잡지 말고 노름하지 말라는 식이다. 부자는 “양반이 겨우 이뿐이냐, 신선 같다더니 너무 밑지는 일이니 이롭게 고쳐 달라”고 청한다.
- 둘째 문서: 사·농·공·상 가운데 선비가 가장 귀하며 양반의 이익이 크다고 시작해, 농사도 장사도 하지 않고 글만 조금 알면 과거에 올라 벼슬하고, 방에는 기생을 두고 뜰에는 곡식을 쌓는다고 쓴다. 가난한 선비도 시골에서는 이웃의 소로 먼저 밭을 갈고 마을 사람을 끌어다 김을 매게 할 수 있으며, 누가 대들면 코에 재를 붓고 상투를 잡아 돌려도 감히 원망하지 못한다고 한다. 부자는 혀를 내밀며 “그만두시오, 맹랑하오. 나를 도둑으로 만들 셈이오”라 하고 고개를 저으며 떠나, 평생 다시는 양반 이야기를 하지 않는다.

**의의**
양반의 허울과 특권, 신분 매매를 풍자한 조선 후기 한문 단편으로 널리 읽힌다. 문서가 두 번 쓰인다는 구성 자체가 양반의 이상(예절·절제)과 현실(특권·횡포)의 간극을 드러낸다.

**읽기 도움**
- 兩班: 문반·무반(東班·西班)을 아울러 이르는 사족. 旌善: 강원도 정선.
- 糶·糴(조·적): 관청 곡식을 꾸어 주고 거두는 환곡의 팔기와 사기. 軍興: 군수 물자.
- 觀察使·郡守: 도 단위·고을 단위 수령.
- 鄕所·座首·別監: 고을의 자치 기구와 그 임원. 通引: 관청 심부름꾼. 戶長: 향리의 우두머리.
- 明文·券: 매매 문서. 乾隆十年은 1745년으로, 이야기 속 가상의 날짜로 보인다.
- 小人: 자신을 낮추는 말. 氈笠: 서민의 벙거지.
- 孟浪: 터무니없음, 엉뚱함.
- ▼(厂+串): 전사자가 입력하지 못한 글자 자리 표시.
notes.en:
**About the author** Park Ji-won (1737–1805, pen name Yeonam), of the Bannam Park clan, came from a distinguished Noron yangban family of Seoul. He gave up the examinations when young and, with Hong Dae-yong, Park Je-ga and Yi Deok-mu, became a leading figure of the Northern Learning (북학) school, which urged learning from Qing China. He hid for a time in Yeonam valley, Hwanghae, to escape Hong Guk-yeong's pressure, which gave him his pen name. In 1780 he went to China with the mission for Emperor Qianlong's seventieth birthday and wrote the Yeolha ilgi. He entered office late by a recommended (eum) appointment and served as magistrate of Anui, Myeoncheon and Yangyang. In Jeongjo's literary-style reform (1792) the Yeolha ilgi's style was criticised and he was reportedly asked for a letter of self-criticism. He died in 1805. 'Yangbanjeon', a satire on the status system, dates from about 1755, when he was roughly 18–20.

**Historical context** 'Yangbanjeon' is an early classical-Chinese story in the Bangyeonggak oejeon; its exact date of writing is not certain, and scholars generally place it around the mid-1750s, when Park was a teenager or in his early twenties. In eighteenth-century Joseon commerce and the money economy were growing and the status system was loosening, and buying yangban standing with money (through grain contributions or genealogy sales) was on the rise. Through a story of a yangban, driven by grain-loan debt, selling his status to a rich man, the work satirises yangban ritualism and privilege. It survives in the Yeonam jip and has been read as showing late Joseon criticism of the status system and the spirit of practical learning.

**Background**
Park Ji-won (1737-1805, pen name Yeonam) was a leading writer of the Northern Learning school in late Joseon. The Yangban-jeon is one tale in the Bangyeonggak oejeon, a volume of his early classical-Chinese stories transmitted as the supplementary collection of the Yeonam jip. The exact date of writing is uncertain; the Wikisource header presents the volume as a collection of early works written in his youth. Scholars generally date it to the mid-1750s, when he was about twenty.

**Contents (the whole edition)**
This edition contains the complete Yangban-jeon, first sentence to last.
- Opening: in Jeongseon county lives a yangban who loves reading; whenever a new magistrate arrives, the magistrate calls on him in person to pay respects. But he is poor and lives on the state grain loans, and over the years the debt reaches 1,000 seok. The touring governor is furious and orders him jailed; the magistrate pities him and cannot bring himself to do it. The yangban weeps day and night, and his wife scolds him: a lifetime of reading is no use against the grain debt, and a yangban is not worth a cent.
- The sale: a rich man of the village reasons that a yangban, though poor, is always honoured, while he, though rich, is held low. He decides to buy the rank and pays the debt. The astonished magistrate visits and finds the yangban in a felt hat and short coat, prostrate in the dirt, calling himself "your humble servant" and saying he has sold his rank. The magistrate praises the rich man and proposes a written deed with the townspeople as witnesses, since a private sale invites lawsuits.
- First deed: the local gentry office, the headman and the overseer witness it. It lists the burdensome duties of a yangban: rise before dawn and recite, endure hunger and cold without mentioning poverty, never handle money or ask the price of rice, do not slaughter cattle or gamble, and so on. The rich man objects that this is all there is to it, when he had heard yangban were like immortals, and asks for a revision in his favour.
- Second deed: it begins by calling the scholar the highest of the four classes, with the greatest advantages. Without farming or trade, a little learning wins office; one keeps singing girls in the rooms and grain in the yard. Even a poor scholar in the country may first plough with a neighbour's ox and make villagers weed his field, and if anyone resists he may pour ash up the man's nose and twist his topknot without fear of complaint. The rich man sticks out his tongue: "Enough, this is absurd! Do you mean to make me a thief?" He shakes his head, leaves, and never speaks of yangban again.

**Significance**
It is widely read as a satire on the yangban's pretensions and privileges and on the trade in status. The twice-written deed itself shows the gap between the yangban ideal (propriety, restraint) and reality (privilege, abuse).

**Reading help**
- 兩班: yangban, the civil (east) and military (west) ranks, the gentry; 旌善: Jeongseon in Gangwon.
- 糶 / 糴: selling and buying grain, here the state grain-loan system; 軍興: military supplies.
- 觀察使 / 郡守: provincial governor / county magistrate.
- 鄕所, 座首, 別監: the local gentry office and its officers; 通引: office runner; 戶長: chief clerk.
- 明文, 券: deed. 乾隆十年 is 1745, probably a fictional date.
- 小人: self-abasing "your humble servant"; 氈笠: commoner's felt hat.
- 孟浪: absurd, reckless.
- ▼(厂+串): placeholder for a character the transcriber could not enter.

paragraphs.orig: 兩班者。士族之尊稱也。旌善之郡。有一兩班。賢而好讀書。每郡守新至。必親造其廬而禮之。然家貧。歲食郡糶。積歲至千石。
paragraphs.reading: 양반자. 사족지존칭야. 정선지군. 유일양반. 현이호독서. 매군수신지. 필친조기려이례지. 연가빈. 세식군조. 적세지천석.
paragraphs.en: “Yangban” is the honorific title of the gentry class. In the county of Jeongseon there lived a certain yangban, a virtuous man who loved to read. Whenever a new magistrate arrived, the magistrate would always go in person to the yangban’s humble house to pay his respects. Yet the household was poor, and year after year he lived on grain borrowed from the county granary. Over the years the debt piled up to a thousand seok.

paragraphs.orig: 觀察使巡行郡邑。閱糶糴。大怒曰。何物兩班。乃乏軍興。命囚其兩班。郡守意哀其兩班貧。無以爲償。不忍囚之。亦無可柰何。兩班日夜泣。計不知所出。其妻罵曰。生平子好讀書。無益縣官糴。咄兩班。兩班不直一錢。
paragraphs.reading: 관찰사순행군읍. 열조적. 대노왈. 하물양반. 내핍군흥. 명수기양반. 군수의애기양반빈. 무이위상. 불인수지. 역무가내하. 양반일야읍. 계부지소출. 기처매왈. 생평자호독서. 무익현관적. 돌양반. 양반부직일전.
paragraphs.en: When the provincial inspector made his tour of the counties and examined the grain-loan ledgers, he flew into a rage. “What kind of yangban is this? He has left the army’s supplies short!” And he ordered the yangban imprisoned. The magistrate pitied the yangban’s poverty, knowing he had no means of repayment, and could not bear to jail him; yet there was nothing he could do either. Day and night the yangban wept, at his wits’ end. His wife scolded him: “All your life you have loved reading, and it has never helped you repay a single measure of the county’s grain. Bah, yangban! Your yangban-hood is not worth a single coin!”

paragraphs.orig: 其里之富人。私相議曰。兩班雖貧。常尊榮。我雖富。常卑賤。不敢騎馬。見兩班則跼蹜屛營。匍匐拜庭。曳鼻膝行。我常如此。其僇辱也。今兩班貧不能償糴。方大窘。其勢誠不能保其兩班。我且買而有之。遂踵門而請償其糴。兩班大喜許諾。
paragraphs.reading: 기리지부인. 사상의왈. 양반수빈. 상존영. 아수부. 상비천. 불감기마. 견양반즉국축병영. 포복배정. 예비슬행. 아상여차. 기륙욕야. 금양반빈불능상적. 방대군. 기세성불능보기양반. 아차매이유지. 수종문이청상기적. 양반대희허락.
paragraphs.en: A rich man of the village, talking it over privately with others, said: “However poor the yangban may be, he is always honoured and esteemed. However rich we may be, we are always low and base. We dare not ride a horse. When we see a yangban we cringe and tremble; we crawl on our bellies and bow in his courtyard, dragging our noses along the ground and shuffling forward on our knees. This is how we always are—it is a lifelong humiliation. Now the yangban is too poor to repay his grain and is in dire straits; truly he cannot hold on to his yangban-hood. I will buy it and have it for myself.” So he went to the yangban’s door and offered to pay off his grain debt. The yangban, overjoyed, agreed.

paragraphs.orig: 於是富人立輸其糴於官。郡守大驚異之。自往勞其兩班。且問償糴狀。兩班氈笠。衣短衣。伏塗謁稱小人。不敢仰視。郡守大驚。下扶曰。足下何自貶辱若是。兩班益恐懼頓首俯伏曰。惶悚小人。非敢自辱。已自鬻其兩班。以償糴。里之富人。乃兩班也。小人復安敢冒其舊號而自尊乎。
paragraphs.reading: 어시부인립수기적어관. 군수대경이지. 자왕로기양반. 차문상적상. 양반전립. 의단의. 복도알칭소인. 불감앙시. 군수대경. 하부왈. 족하하자폄욕약시. 양반익공구돈수부복왈. 황송소인. 비감자욕. 이자육기양반. 이상적. 이지부인. 내양반야. 소인부안감모기구호이자존호.
paragraphs.en: Thereupon the rich man at once delivered the grain to the government. The magistrate was astonished, and went himself to console the yangban and to ask how the debt had been repaid. The yangban, in a felt hat and a short jacket, was prostrate in the dirt to greet him, calling himself “your humble servant” and not daring to look up. The magistrate, greatly startled, came down and helped him up, saying, “Sir, why do you degrade and shame yourself like this?” The yangban, more terrified than ever, knocked his head on the ground and bowed low: “I tremble, your servant. I would never dare to disgrace myself. I have already sold my yangban-hood to repay the grain. The rich man of the village is the yangban now. How could your servant presume to use his old title and put on airs?”

paragraphs.orig: 郡守歎曰。君子哉富人也。兩班哉富人也。富而不吝。義也。急人之難。仁也。惡卑而慕尊。智也。此眞兩班。雖然。私自交易而不立券。訟之端也。我與汝。約郡人而證之。立券而信之。郡守當自署之。
paragraphs.reading: 군수탄왈. 군자재부인야. 양반재부인야. 부이불린. 의야. 급인지난. 인야. 오비이모존. 지야. 차진양반. 수연. 사자교역이불립권. 송지단야. 아여여. 약군인이증지. 입권이신지. 군수당자서지.
paragraphs.en: The magistrate sighed: “What a gentleman this rich man is! What a yangban! To be rich yet not miserly—that is righteousness. To hurry to the aid of another in trouble—that is benevolence. To hate lowliness and yearn for honour—that is wisdom. This is a true yangban. Even so, to trade privately without drawing up a deed is the beginning of lawsuits. You and I shall gather the people of the county to bear witness, and draw up a deed to make it binding. I, the magistrate, shall sign it myself.”

paragraphs.orig: 於是郡守歸府。悉召郡中之士族及農工商賈。悉至于庭。富人坐鄕所之右。兩班立於公兄之下。乃爲立券曰。
paragraphs.reading: 어시군수귀부. 실소군중지사족급농공상고. 실지우정. 부인좌향소지우. 양반립어공형지하. 내위립권왈.
paragraphs.en: The magistrate returned to his office and summoned all the gentry of the county, together with the farmers, artisans and merchants; they all assembled in the courtyard. The rich man was seated on the right side of the hyangso (the local gentry council), while the yangban stood below the three senior clerks (gonghyeong). A deed was then drawn up, which read:

paragraphs.orig: 乾隆十年九月日。右明文段。▼(厂+串)賣兩班爲償官糓。其直千斛。維厥兩班。名謂多端。讀書曰士。從政爲大夫。有德爲君子。武階列西。文秩叙東。是爲兩班。
paragraphs.reading: 건륭십년구월일. 우명문단. 환매양반위상관곡. 기치천곡. 유궐양반. 명위다단. 독서왈사. 종정위대부. 유덕위군자. 무계열서. 문질서동. 시위양반.
paragraphs.en: “Year 10 of Qianlong [1745], ninth month, on such-and-such a day. This deed of record: the yangban-hood is hereby sold to repay the government grain; its price is one thousand seok. This yangban goes by many names: one who reads books is called a scholar; one who enters government service is a grandee; one of virtue is a gentleman. The military ranks line up on the west, the civil ranks on the east: these are the two orders—the yangban.

paragraphs.orig: 任爾所從。絶棄鄙事。希古尙志。五更常起。點硫燃脂。目視鼻端。會踵支尻。東萊博議。誦如氷瓢。忍饑耐寒。口不說貧。叩齒彈腦。細嗽嚥津。袖刷毳冠。拂塵生波。盥無擦拳。漱口無過。長聲喚婢。緩步曳履。
paragraphs.reading: 임이소종. 절기비사. 희고상지. 오경상기. 점류연지. 목시비단. 회종지고. 동래박의. 송여빙표. 인기내한. 구불설빈. 고치탄뇌. 세수연진. 수쇄취관. 불진생파. 관무찰권. 수구무과. 장성환비. 완보예리.
paragraphs.en: Follow whichever you choose. Cast aside all base affairs; emulate the ancients and set your will high. Always rise at the fifth watch; strike a light with sulphur and burn the oil lamp. Fix your eyes on the tip of your nose; sit with your heels together and your buttocks propped on them. Recite the Dongnae Bagui (Lü Zuqian’s “Donglai Boyi”) as smoothly as ice rolling in a gourd. Bear hunger and endure cold; never speak of poverty. Click your teeth and flick the back of your skull; cough softly and swallow your saliva. Brush your fur hat with your sleeve until the dust ripples like waves. When washing, do not rub with your fist; when rinsing your mouth, do not overdo it. Call your maid in a long-drawn voice; walk slowly, dragging your shoes.

paragraphs.orig: 古文眞寶。唐詩品彙。鈔寫如荏。一行百字。手毋執錢。不問米價。暑毋跣襪。飯毋徒髻。食毋先羹。歠毋流聲。下箸毋舂。毋餌生葱。飮醪毋嘬鬚。吸煙毋輔窳。忿毋搏妻。怒毋踢器。毋拳敺兒女。毋詈死奴僕。叱牛馬。毋辱鬻主。病毋招巫。祭不齋僧。爐不煑手。語不齒唾。毋屠牛。毋賭錢。
paragraphs.reading: 고문진보. 당시품휘. 초사여임. 일행백자. 수무집전. 불문미가. 서무선말. 반무도계. 식무선갱. 철무류성. 하저무용. 무이생총. 음료무최수. 흡연무보유. 분무박처. 노무척기. 무권구아녀. 무리사노복. 질우마. 무욕육주. 병무초무. 제부재승. 노부자수. 어불치타. 무도우. 무도전.
paragraphs.en: Copy out the Gomun Jinbo and the Dangsi Pumhwi, writing as small as perilla seeds, a hundred characters to a line. Never hold money in your hand; never ask the price of rice. In summer do not go barefoot; at meals do not leave your topknot bare. Do not take your soup before your rice; do not slurp when you sip; do not pound with your chopsticks; do not eat raw scallions; when drinking rice wine, do not suck your whiskers; when smoking, do not hollow your cheeks. In anger do not strike your wife; in rage do not kick the dishes; do not beat your children with your fists; do not curse dead servants; when scolding oxen and horses, do not revile the man who sold them. When ill, do not call a shaman; at sacrifices, do not engage monks to hold a rite; do not warm your hands at the brazier; when you talk, do not let spittle pass your teeth; do not slaughter oxen; do not gamble for money.

paragraphs.orig: 凡此百行。有違兩班。持此文記。卞正于官城主。旌善郡守押。座首別監證署。
paragraphs.reading: 범차백행. 유위양반. 지차문기. 변정우관성주. 정선군수압. 좌수별감증서.
paragraphs.en: If in any of these hundred practices you fall short of a yangban, take this document to the authorities and have the matter judged before the lord of the city. Signed: the magistrate of Jeongseon. Witnessed and signed: the jwasu (head of the hyangso) and the byeolgam (his assistant).”

paragraphs.orig: 於是通引搨印錯落。聲中嚴皷。斗縱參橫。戶長讀旣畢。富人悵然久之曰。兩班只此而已耶。吾聞兩班如神仙。審如是。太乾沒。願改爲可利。
paragraphs.reading: 어시통인탑인착락. 성중엄고. 두종삼횡. 호장독기필. 부인창연구지왈. 양반지차이이야. 오문양반여신선. 심여시. 태건몰. 원개위가리.
paragraphs.en: Then the magistrate’s attendants (tongin) stamped the seals, crisscrossing the page; amid the sound of the solemn drum, the seals fell like the Dipper upright and Orion athwart. When the head clerk had finished reading, the rich man, dismayed, stood silent a long while, then said: “Is this all there is to being a yangban? I had heard that yangban were like immortals. If this is really all, it is far too poor a bargain. I beg you to change it into something more profitable.”

paragraphs.orig: 於是乃更作券曰。維天生民。其民維四。四民之中。最貴者士。稱以兩班。利莫大矣。不耕不商。粗涉文史。大决文科。小成進士。文科紅牌。不過二尺。百物備具。維錢之槖。進士三十。乃筮初仕。猶爲名蔭。善事雄南。耳白傘風。腹皤鈴諾。室珥冶妓。庭糓鳴鶴。窮士居鄕。猶能武斷。先耕隣牛。借耘里氓。孰敢慢我。灰灌汝鼻。暈髻汰鬢。無敢怨咨。
paragraphs.reading: 어시내경작권왈. 유천생민. 기민유사. 사민지중. 최귀자사. 칭이양반. 이막대의. 불경불상. 조섭문사. 대결문과. 소성진사. 문과홍패. 불과이척. 백물비구. 유전지탁. 진사삼십. 내서초사. 유위명음. 선사웅남. 이백산풍. 복파령낙. 실이야기. 정곡명학. 궁사거향. 유능무단. 선경인우. 차운이맹. 숙감만아. 회관여비. 훈계태빈. 무감원자.
paragraphs.en: So a new deed was drawn up: “Heaven gave birth to the people, and the people are four. Among the four, the most honoured is the scholar, who is called yangban; no gain is greater than this. He neither ploughs nor trades; with a rough acquaintance with letters and histories, at best he passes the civil examination, at the least he becomes a jinsa. The red certificate of the civil examination is no more than two feet long, yet it provides a hundred things—it is a very bag of money. A jinsa at thirty is divined for his first post, and even at the worst he becomes a man of repute by hereditary privilege (eum). If he serves well, he rises to a grand “southern” post: his ears whitened by the wind of the parasol borne over him, his belly swelling as the bell is rung and the servants answer “Yes, sir”; in his chambers courtesans wear earrings, in his courtyard cranes cry over the grain he scatters. And a poor scholar living in the country can still lord it over others: he ploughs first with a neighbour’s ox, and borrows the villagers to weed his fields. Who dares slight me? I will pour ash up your nose, twist your topknot round and pluck out your side-locks—and no one dares complain.”

paragraphs.orig: 富人中其券而吐舌曰。已之已之。孟浪哉。將使我爲盜耶。掉頭而去。終身不復言兩班之事。
paragraphs.reading: 부인중기권이토설왈. 이지이지. 맹랑재. 장사아위도야. 도두이거. 종신불부언양반지사.
paragraphs.en: Halfway through the deed, the rich man stuck out his tongue and said: “Enough, enough! How preposterous! Would you make a robber of me?” Shaking his head, he left, and for the rest of his life never spoke again of yangban matters.

review.notes: Right work: complete 兩班傳 as a single paragraph (ends at the true last sentence). Card and notes rewritten from the volume to the tale itself; the date is hedged (catalogue c.1780 not asserted) and the plot checked line by line against the text. validate.py reports no en for the explicit original-only paragraph, as expected. Author/context sections added 2026-10-08 and fact-checked by an independent reviewer (batch 1). Translation (2026-11-03) reviewed by an independent content-review agent: Checked all 14 paragraphs against the Classical Chinese: no omissions or additions found; names, numbers (1000 seok, Qianlong 10 = 1745) and negations correct. Readings: fixed 2 (불직->부직), 9 (제불재승->제부재승, 로불자수->노부자수) for the 不 before ㅈ and sentence-initial 두음 rule; others standard. English fixes: 6 (hyangso/gonghyeong glossed), 8 (Dongnae Bagui glossed), 10 (座首/別監 rendered as jwasu/byeolgam instead of 'district head/inspector'), 11 (通引 = magistrate's attendants), 12 (eum privilege; 腹皤鈴諾 corrected: bell is rung, servants answer), 13 (中其券 = halfway through the deed). Paragraph breaks fall at sensible scene boundaries (debt, inspector, rich man's offer, visit, magistrate's speech, assembly, deed 1 in three parts, reaction, deed 2, ending). Remaining doubts: the odd glyph before 賣 in para 7 (reading 환 is a guess; sense 'sold' is secure); 名蔭, 善事雄南 and 暈髻汰鬢 are obscure and rendered by best sense.
